description: Per-translation glossary overlay for the Wheel of Heaven Translation of 2 Samuel (canon-cited chapter 6, wave MC). v1.0.0 (2026-11-02, Wave MC, Hebrew part (Josh 3; Judg 7; 2 Sam 6; Editor pass 2026-11-02, claude-opus-5-5)) creates the overlay. It holds the nine Former Prophets conventions shared verbatim (identical text and identical appliesTo, the union over the four books) with the joshua-woh, judges-woh and 1-samuel-woh overlays: Hebrew proper-name transliteration, the elohim referent/article rule, the 'man of the Elohim' title, the nefesh scope, the ruach transliteration, Ketiv/Qere, the MT baseline, 'YHWH of hosts' and Ba'al; extend all four together. Book-specific decisions: yōšēḇ hakkəruḇîm 'who is enthroned on the cherubim' (6:2) and the single-site cruxes of 2 Sam 6 (6:1 'gathered', 6:5 the MT 'instruments of fir-wood' and the ASV instrument names, 6:6 'reached out' without supplement and 'stumbled', 6:7 'for his error', 6:19 'a portion of meat', 6:21 'prince'). No speculative entry; the canon's reading of the ark appears only in a labelled reception note. Central proposals in leviticus-woh/wave-mc-he-central-diff.json. Wave MC signed off at human review on 2026-11-02 (zarazinsfuss); its central proposals were applied as central glossary v2.91.0 (New Testament), v2.92.0 (Septuagint) and v2.93.0 (Hebrew).

entries.wohChoice: WoH transliteration of the Hebrew name, under the founder-ratified Kings convention (1-kings-woh / 2-kings-woh `hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`, ratified at human sign-off 2026-11-01): Hebrew long forms; tz for tsade; ʿayin and aleph marked with an apostrophe where the Kings table does; gentilics in -î take English '-ite' on the transliterated stem; a small set of names fixed in English usage is kept in English (here Gilgal, David, Asherah, the Levites); and each chapter title adds the English form of its principal name in parentheses. Equivalence table. Joshua 5, 6, 10: Yehoshua = Joshua; Nun = Nun; Yarden = Jordan; Yericho = Jericho; Mitzrayim = Egypt; Kena'an = Canaan; Yisra'el = Israel; Rachav = Rahab; Adoni-Tzedeq = Adoni-zedek; Yerushalayim = Jerusalem; Giv'on = Gibeon; Hevron = Hebron; Pir'am = Piram; Yarmut = Jarmuth; Yafia = Japhia; Lakhish = Lachish; Devir = Debir; Beit-Choron = Beth-horon; Azeqah = Azekah; Maqqedah = Makkedah; Ayyalon = Aijalon; Livnah = Libnah; Qadesh-Barnea = Kadesh-barnea; Azzah = Gaza; the Negev (hanneḡeḇ; ASV 'the South'); Ai, Hoham, Eglon, Horam, Gezer and Goshen are identical in both forms; gentilics 'the Emorites' (hāʾĕmōrî; ASV 'the Amorites') and 'the Kena'anites' (hakkənaʿănî; ASV 'the Canaanites'); the descriptive toponym gibʿaṯ hāʿărālôṯ is translated 'the hill of the foreskins' (ASV). Judges 6, 13: Midyan = Midian; Amaleq = Amalek; Ofrah = Ophrah; Yo'ash = Joash; Avi'ezer = Abiezer, 'the Avi'ezrite(s)' = the Abiezrite(s); Gid'on = Gideon; Menasheh = Manasseh; Zevulun = Zebulun; Naftali = Naphtali; Yizre'el = Jezreel; Yerubba'al = Jerubbaal; the altar name YHWH-Shalom = Jehovah-shalom (as genesis-woh 'YHWH-yir'eh', Gen 22:14); Tzor'ah = Zorah; 'the Danites'; Manoach = Manoah; Shimshon = Samson; Machaneh-Dan = Mahaneh-dan; Eshta'ol = Eshtaol; Asher identical; bənê-qeḏem translated 'the children of the east' (ASV). 1 Samuel 3, 5, 6, 17: Shemu'el = Samuel; Be'er Sheva = Beersheba (central be-er-sheva-folk-etymology); Even-Ha'ezer = Eben-ezer; 'the Ashdodites'; Gat = Gath; Eqron = Ekron, 'the Eqronites'; Par'oh = Pharaoh (as Kings); Beit-Shemesh = Beth-shemesh, 'the Beit-Shimshite' = the Beth-shemite; Ashqelon = Ashkelon; Qiryat-Ye'arim = Kiriath-jearim; Golyat = Goliath; Sha'ul = Saul; Yishai = Jesse; Eli'av = Eliab; Avinadav = Abinadab; Avner = Abner; Beit-Lechem = Bethlehem, 'the Beit-Lechemite' = the Bethlehemite, 'the Efratite' = the Ephrathite; Yehudah = Judah; Sokhoh = Socoh; Efes-Dammim = Ephes-dammim; Sha'arayim = Shaaraim; Eli, Dan, Shiloh, Ashdod, Dagon (central dagon entry), Shammah, Elah and Gai are identical in both forms. Pelishtim: the plural pəlištîm is 'the Pelishtim' as fixed by the central pelishtim-caphtor entry; the singular gentilic happəlištî is 'the Pelishtite' under the '-ite' rule (ASV 'the Philistines' / 'the Philistine'). Wave MC (Josh 3; Judg 7; 2 Sam 6). Joshua 3: Shittim (mēhaššiṭṭîm, with the article; ASV 'Shittim'; the Torah volumes print the full name 'Avel-haShittim', Num 33:49); Adam (the city, 3:16); Tzaretan = Zarethan; 'the Sea of the Aravah, the Salt Sea' = the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea; Moshe = Moses; the seven peoples of 3:10 as plurals under the '-ite' rule, as Josh 5:1: 'the Kena'anites, the Chittites, the Chivvites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Emorites, the Yevusites' (ASV the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Hivite, the Perizzite, the Girgashite, the Amorite, the Jebusite). Judges 7: Charod = Harod (ʿên ḥărōḏ 'the spring of Charod'); Moreh (giḇʿaṯ hammôreh 'the hill of Moreh'); Purah; Beit-haShittah = Beth-shittah; Tzererah = Zererah; Avel-Mecholah = Abel-meholah; Tabbat = Tabbath; Beit-Barah = Beth-barah; Efrayim = Ephraim; Gil'ad = Gilead; Orev = Oreb; Ze'ev = Zeeb; the descriptive toponyms ṣûr-ʿôrēḇ and yeqeḇ-zəʾēḇ are translated 'the rock of Orev' and 'the winepress of Ze'ev' (ASV), as gibʿaṯ hāʿărālôṯ is. 2 Samuel 6: Ba'alei-Yehudah = Baale-judah; Uzzah (the MT alternates ʿuzzāʾ, vv 3, 6, and ʿuzzâ, vv 7-8; one English form); Achyo = Ahio; Nakhon = Nacon; Oved-Edom = Obed-edom, 'the Gittite' = the Gittite (Gat + '-ite'); Mikhal = Michal; Peretz-Uzzah = Perez-uzzah (unglossed, the pāraṣ / pereṣ play given in commentary under central peretz-breach-davidic-ancestor-etymology); David, Sha'ul, Avinadav, Yisra'el and Yehudah as above.
entries.rationale: Former Prophets wave 1 (Josh 5, 6, 10; Judg 6, 13; 1 Sam 3, 5, 6, 17; Editor pass 2026-11-01, claude-opus-5-5). This entry is shared verbatim by the joshua-woh, judges-woh, 1-samuel-woh and 2-samuel-woh overlays; extend all four together. It applies, without change of substance, the Kings name convention that the founder ratified on 2026-11-01 (1-kings-woh / 2-kings-woh `hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`). The reasons given there hold for Joshua, Judges and Samuel, which continue the same narrative Hebrew: the corpus renders the Torah narratives and Kings with transliterated name forms (genesis-woh, exodus-woh, Kings), so the books between them should not switch to the KJV forms; transliteration keeps the theophoric and meaningful elements visible, which these chapters use (Yehoshua 'YHWH saves'; Shemu'el; the Ba'al element of Yerubba'al, which Judg 6:32 explains; Shimshon beside Beit-Shemesh, 'house of the sun'); and every name is given with its conventional English equivalent in this table and in the commentary at first occurrence in each chapter, so a reader can match the translation to the ASV and to the English editions of the Raëlian books, which quote these chapters as 'Joshua', 'Gideon', 'Samuel' and 'Goliath'. The convention is presentational and carries no interpretive content. Former Prophets specifics: (a) Azzah (Gaza) is transliterated, because it is not one of the few names that Kings keeps in English (Moab, Aram, Damascus, Horeb, Gilgal). (b) hanneḡeḇ is the region 'the Negev', where the ASV's 'the South' reads as a compass direction. (c) Gentilics follow the Kings '-ite' rule ('the Tishbite', 'the Shunammite', 'the Shomronites'): 'the Emorites', 'the Kena'anites', 'the Avi'ezrite', 'the Danites', 'the Ashdodites', 'the Eqronites', 'the Beit-Shimshite', 'the Pelishtite'. The corpus is not yet uniform on gentilics: genesis-woh writes 'the Emori', 'the Kena'ani' under central ten-nations-of-canaan (Gen 15:19-21), exodus-woh writes 'the Amorite', 'the Canaanite', and the plural 'Pelishtim' follows central pelishtim-caphtor (Gen 10:14), so the singular 'the Pelishtite' and the plural 'the Pelishtim' differ in form. A corpus-wide decision is a founder point in the wave-FP1 editor report; whichever form is chosen, the change is a mechanical substitution. (d) gibʿaṯ hāʿărālôṯ (Josh 5:3) is translated, as in the ASV, because it is a descriptive designation that the narrative explains, while Gilgal (5:9), whose explanation is a wordplay, stays a name. (e) Altar names are transliterated as names (YHWH-Shalom, Judg 6:24), with the meaning in commentary, as genesis-woh does for YHWH-yir'eh. Ratified at human sign-off (2026-11-01, zarazinsfuss), Former Prophets wave 1: the Former Prophets keep transliterated names with '-ite' gentilics, as Kings; the names stay split by book family for now (Torah English forms as published Exodus; Prophets and Writings English forms), with one corpus-wide naming decision later. Wave MC, Hebrew part (Josh 3; Judg 7; 2 Sam 6; Editor pass 2026-11-02, claude-opus-5-5) extends the table with the names of Josh 3, Judg 7 and 2 Sam 6; 2-samuel-woh, a new book, now carries the shared set.

entries.wohChoice: The five clauses of the founder-ratified Kings entry `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`, unchanged, plus two clauses for constructions Kings did not meet. (1) YHWH referent with the Hebrew article (hāʾĕlōhîm): 'the Elohim' (Judg 6:20 'the messenger of the Elohim'; 6:36, 39; 13:6, 8, 9; 1 Sam 5:1, 2, 10, 11 'the ark of the Elohim', 5:11 'the hand of the Elohim'; 6:20 'YHWH, this holy Elohim', where the demonstrative stands for the article). (2) YHWH referent, anarthrous predicate, genitive or subject in direct speech: 'Elohim' without article (Judg 13:5, 7 'a Nazirite to Elohim'; 13:22 'we have seen Elohim', as genesis-woh Gen 32:31; 1 Sam 3:3 'the lamp of Elohim', 'the ark of Elohim'; 3:17 the Israelite oath 'So may Elohim do to you', as 1 Kgs 2:23; 17:46 'there is Elohim in Yisra'el', as 2 Kgs 1:3). (3) Construct with a possessor: 'YHWH your Elohim' (Josh 10:19; Judg 6:10, 26), 'the Elohim of Yisra'el' (Josh 10:40, 42; Judg 6:8; 1 Sam 5:7, 8, 10, 11; 6:3, 5), 'the Elohim of the armies of Yisra'el' (1 Sam 17:45). (4) Non-YHWH referent: lower-case 'elohim', number following the Hebrew ('the elohim of the Emorites', Judg 6:10; 'If he is an elohim', 6:31, of Ba'al; 'Dagon our elohim', 1 Sam 5:7; 'your elohim', 6:5; 'by his elohim', 17:43). (5) Generic class in a comparison or negation: lower-case 'elohim' (no site in this wave). (6) New: anarthrous ʾĕlōhîm as the subject of a narrative clause takes the article of the central elohim-as-translation narrative rule: 'And the Elohim did so' (Judg 6:40, wayyaʿaś ʾĕlōhîm kēn), the Hebrew difference from the articular vv 36, 39 being recorded in commentary. (7) New: anarthrous ʾĕlōhîm with an attributive adjective takes an English determiner, which English grammar requires: 'the armies of the living Elohim' (1 Sam 17:26, 36, maʿarḵôṯ ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm), with the anarthrous Hebrew and the plural adjective recorded in commentary. Wave MC sites: clause (1) 'the ark of the Elohim' (2 Sam 6:2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 12) and 'the Elohim struck him' (6:7, articular narrative subject); 'into his hand the Elohim has given Midyan' (Judg 7:14, articular, in the mouth of a Midyanite); clause (3) 'YHWH your Elohim' (Josh 3:3, 9). (8) New: bare ʾēl is transliterated 'El', as in the Torah overlays (clause 5 of elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-torah) and the central El-compounds (el-elyon, el-shaddai), and takes an English determiner with an attributive adjective, as in clause (7): 'the living El' (Josh 3:10, ʾēl ḥay; ASV 'the living God').
entries.rationale: Former Prophets wave 1 (Josh 5, 6, 10; Judg 6, 13; 1 Sam 3, 5, 6, 17; Editor pass 2026-11-01, claude-opus-5-5). This entry is shared verbatim by the joshua-woh, judges-woh, 1-samuel-woh and 2-samuel-woh overlays; extend all four together. The Kings entry (ratified 2026-11-01) supplements the central elohim-as-translation convention, which keeps the plural 'Elohim' untranslated and sets the narrative article, with a referent rule: a capital for YHWH and lower case for any other god, so that contrasts the narrative depends on stay visible (Carmel, 1 Kgs 18; Ba'al-Zevuv, 2 Kgs 1). Judges and Samuel are built on the same contrast: Yo'ash's 'If he is an elohim, let him contend for himself' (Judg 6:31) answers the Ba'al cult as Eliyahu's 'for he is an elohim' does (1 Kgs 18:27), and 1 Sam 5 sets 'Dagon our elohim' (5:7) against the ark of 'the Elohim of Yisra'el'. The article follows the Hebrew in predicate, genitive and direct-speech positions, since adding 'the' there turns a classifying expression into an identification the Hebrew does not make (BDB ʾĕlōhîm 3). Two constructions occur here that Kings did not meet. (6) The Kings entry states that 'the narrative-subject article rule of the central entry is unaffected', and its anarthrous clause covers predicates, genitives and subjects in direct speech; an anarthrous narrative subject (Judg 6:40, after articular hāʾĕlōhîm in vv 36, 39) therefore falls under the central narrative rule and is rendered 'the Elohim'. The two Hebrew forms then look alike in English, and the commentary records the difference; dropping the article in narrative would reintroduce the singular proper-name reading the central entry was written to avoid. (7) maʿarḵôṯ ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm (1 Sam 17:26, 36; cf. Deut 5:23 [ET 5:26]; Jer 10:10; 23:36) is anarthrous, but an English attributive adjective needs a determiner ('the armies of living Elohim' is not idiomatic English), so the article is supplied as the ASV does ('the living God'); the commentary records that the Hebrew has no article and that the adjective ḥayyîm is plural in agreement with the form ʾĕlōhîm, unlike ʾēl ḥay (Josh 3:10; Hos 2:1 [ET 1:10]). The capital/lower-case distinction is an editorial device, since Hebrew script has no case. Wave MC, Hebrew part (Josh 3; Judg 7; 2 Sam 6; Editor pass 2026-11-02, claude-opus-5-5): Josh 3:10 has ʾēl ḥay, the singular ʾēl with a singular adjective, which the clause (7) rationale already distinguishes from the plural-agreement ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm; English 'God' would merge two different Hebrew words, so ʾēl is transliterated as elsewhere in the corpus (clause 8), and the commentary records the construction (Hos 2:1 [ET 1:10]; Ps 42:3; 84:3). At Judg 7:14 the speaker is a Midyanite, but the narrator presents his dream as the sign YHWH promised Gid'on (7:9-11) and the deity he names is the one who gives Midyan into Gid'on's hand, so clause (1) applies, as clause (3) does to Pelishti speech at 1 Sam 5:7; clause (4) would imply a generic deity the narrative does not intend.

entries.literal: man of the God / a man of God
entries.standardEnglish: man of God (ASV, KJV, NRSV, NJPS)
entries.wohChoice: As the founder-ratified Kings entry `ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`: 'man of the Elohim' where the Hebrew has the article, 'a man of Elohim' where it does not. Sites in this wave: 'The man of the Elohim came to me' (Judg 13:6; ASV 'A man of God') and 'let the man of the Elohim whom you sent come again' (13:8), both articular.
entries.rationale: Former Prophets wave 1 (Josh 5, 6, 10; Judg 6, 13; 1 Sam 3, 5, 6, 17; Editor pass 2026-11-01, claude-opus-5-5). This entry is shared verbatim by the joshua-woh, judges-woh, 1-samuel-woh and 2-samuel-woh overlays; extend all four together. ʾîš (hā)ʾĕlōhîm designates a person who belongs to and acts for the deity (BDB ʾîš 5); Kings uses it of Eliyahu, Elisha and the prophet of 1 Kgs 13, and the central elohim-as-translation convention excludes the rendering 'man of God'. The Kings entry renders the Hebrew article where it stands, because the alternation carries meaning in 2 Kgs 1:9-13, and records that the article on the genitive makes the whole chain definite (GKC §127a; Joüon-Muraoka §139a). In Judg 13:6 Manoach's wife uses the articular title at the first mention, before she knows what the figure is, and then compares his appearance with that of 'the messenger of the Elohim'. The definite English 'The man of the Elohim' follows the Hebrew; the ASV's indefinite 'A man of God' is a defensible English idiom for a first mention, and the commentary records it. The title used here of the figure later identified as the malʾaḵ YHWH (13:16, 21) is the same title Kings uses of human prophets, and the translation does not decide between the two by its rendering.

entries.lemma: nepeš 'throat, breath, life, living being, self'
entries.standardEnglish: soul (Josh 10:28-39, 'all the souls'; 1 Sam 17:55 'as thy soul liveth', ASV)
entries.wohChoice: As the founder-ratified Kings entry `nefesh-scope-and-spelling-kings`: 'nefesh' (transliterated) only where the nepeš is named as the life-component that departs or returns; idiomatic English elsewhere. Sites in this wave: 'every person that was in it' for kol-hannep̄eš ʾăšer-bāh (Josh 10:28, 30, 32, 35, 37 twice, 39; ASV 'all the souls'); 'As you yourself live' for the oath ḥê-nap̄šəḵā (1 Sam 17:55; ASV 'As thy soul liveth'), as 2 Kgs 2:2, 4, 6; 4:30.
entries.rationale: Former Prophets wave 1 (Josh 5, 6, 10; Judg 6, 13; 1 Sam 3, 5, 6, 17; Editor pass 2026-11-01, claude-opus-5-5). This entry is shared verbatim by the joshua-woh, judges-woh, 1-samuel-woh and 2-samuel-woh overlays; extend all four together. nepeš covers throat, breath, appetite, life, living being and the person him- or herself (HALOT nepeš 1-9; Wolff, Anthropology of the Old Testament, 1974), and the central glossary rejects the Platonic 'soul' for it (nefesh-chayah). The Kings entry transliterates it only where it names the life that leaves or returns to the body (1 Kgs 17:21-22, with central tzet-nephesh-departure-at-death-formula) and renders the idioms in English. In the conquest formula kol-hannep̄eš ʾăšer-bāh (Josh 10:28-39; 11:11) nepeš is the individual living being, the persons in a captured city (HALOT 'person'; NRSV 'every person in it'), so 'every person' renders it without the ASV's 'souls', which would suggest a technical sense the formula does not have. The oath ḥê-nap̄šəḵā swears by the addressee's life and is rendered 'as you yourself live' (cf. NJPS 'as you live'), the Kings rendering at 2 Kgs 2:2, 4, 6 and 4:30. The house spelling 'nefesh' (f for the spirantized p) is that of the Kings entry; no transliterated site occurs in this wave.

entries.literal: the wind/breath/spirit of YHWH; (a person's) spirit
entries.standardEnglish: the Spirit of Jehovah came upon (Judg 6:34), began to move (13:25) (ASV); there was no spirit in them any more (Josh 5:1, ASV)
entries.wohChoice: As the founder-ratified Kings entry `ruach-yhwh-and-prophetic-ruach-transliteration-kings`: 'the ruach of YHWH' for rûaḥ YHWH as an agent acting on a person (Kings: 1 Kgs 18:12; 22:24; 2 Kgs 2:16). Sites in this wave: 'But the ruach of YHWH clothed Gid'on' (Judg 6:34; the verb lāḇəšâ rendered literally, ASV 'came upon') and 'And the ruach of YHWH began to move him' (Judg 13:25; pāʿam 'move', ASV). The human rûaḥ in the sense of courage or vital energy is translated 'spirit' in lower case: 'there was no more spirit in them' (Josh 5:1; cf. 1 Kgs 10:5).
entries.rationale: Former Prophets wave 1 (Josh 5, 6, 10; Judg 6, 13; 1 Sam 3, 5, 6, 17; Editor pass 2026-11-01, claude-opus-5-5). This entry is shared verbatim by the joshua-woh, judges-woh, 1-samuel-woh and 2-samuel-woh overlays; extend all four together. rûaḥ covers 'wind', 'breath' and 'spirit' (BDB; HALOT rûaḥ 1-11). The ASV capital 'Spirit of Jehovah' settles the reading in favour of the later doctrinal concept of a personal Holy Spirit, which the Hebrew does not specify; the Kings entry, ratified at human sign-off on 2026-11-01, therefore transliterates rûaḥ YHWH as 'the ruach of YHWH' wherever it is an agent acting on a person, as ezekiel-woh does at Ezek 37:1, and it is applied here so that the same expression reads alike across the Former Prophets. In Judges the rûaḥ YHWH is the power that comes on a deliverer and moves him to act (Block, Judges, Ruth, NAC 6, 1999; Webb, The Book of Judges, NICOT, 2012), and the book uses distinct verbs for its coming: hāyâ ʿal 'came upon' (3:10; 11:29), ṣālaḥ ʿal 'rushed upon' (14:6, 19; 15:14), lāḇaš 'clothed' (6:34) and pāʿam 'move, impel' (13:25). The translation keeps the noun constant and the verbs distinct. lāḇəšâ ʾeṯ-giḏʿôn is rendered literally 'clothed Gid'on', as the KJV margin and many commentators do (the rûaḥ takes the person as its garment; cf. 1 Chr 12:19; 2 Chr 24:20), instead of the ASV's levelling 'came upon'; pāʿam (13:25), whose noun means 'a beat, a step', keeps the ASV 'move'. The anthropological rûaḥ of Josh 5:1, the courage that fails the kings of Kena'an, is an ordinary English sense of 'spirit' and is translated. The entry is inferred, as its Kings source is: transliteration leaves a recognized ambiguity open, and the commentary sets out the readings without choosing.

entries.lemma: Ketiv ('what is written', the consonantal text) and Qere ('what is read', the Masoretic reading tradition)
entries.literal: the written consonants vs the vocalized reading
entries.standardEnglish: ASV and all major English versions translate the Qere, with occasional exceptions
entries.wohChoice: As the founder-ratified Kings entry `ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`: translate the Qere; record the Ketiv in commentary at every site. Sites in this wave (15 readings in 15 verses, as marked in the source edition): Josh 5:1 (K ʿbrnw 'we crossed' / Q ʿoḇrām 'they crossed'), 6:5 (K bə- / Q kə- 'when you hear'), 6:7 (K 'and they said' / Q 'and he said'), 6:9 (K perfect tqʿw / Q participle tōqəʿê 'who blew'), 6:13 (K participle / Q infinitive absolute hālôḵ); Judg 6:5 (K ybʾw, imperfect yāḇōʾû / Q ûḇāʾû), 13:17 (K 'your words' / Q 'your word'); 1 Sam 3:2 (K 'his eye' / Q 'his eyes'), 5:6, 5:9, 5:12, 6:4, 6:5 (K ʿŏp̄ālîm 'swellings' / Q ṭəḥōrîm 'tumors', governed also by `ofalim-tehorim-tumors-1-samuel-5-6`), 17:7 (K wḥṣ / Q wəʿēṣ 'shaft'), 17:23 (K 'from the caves' / Q 'from the ranks'). Wave MC sites (4 readings in 4 verses; none in 2 Sam 6): Josh 3:4 (K wbynw / Q ûḇênāyw 'and between it', spelling only), 3:16 (K bʾdm 'at Adam' / Q mēʾāḏām 'from Adam'; the ASV follows K); Judg 7:13 (K ṣlwl / Q ṣəlîl 'a round loaf', spelling only), 7:21 (K wyynysw, Hiphil 'and they put to flight' / Q wayyānûsû 'and they fled'; the ASV follows K).
entries.rationale: Former Prophets wave 1 (Josh 5, 6, 10; Judg 6, 13; 1 Sam 3, 5, 6, 17; Editor pass 2026-11-01, claude-opus-5-5). This entry is shared verbatim by the joshua-woh, judges-woh, 1-samuel-woh and 2-samuel-woh overlays; extend all four together. The Leningrad Codex marks each Ketiv/Qere pair, and the Masoretic tradition reads the Qere; English translation, including the ASV baseline, follows the Qere in all but a handful of cases (Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible, 3rd ed., 2012). The Kings entry, ratified 2026-11-01, translates the Qere and records the Ketiv, so that the English follows the reading tradition and the consonantal text stays auditable. Of the fifteen readings here, three depart from the ASV, which follows the Ketiv at Josh 5:1 ('until we were passed over'), 6:7 ('And they said') and Judg 13:17 ('thy words'); the Qere is translated there as everywhere and the ASV reading is recorded in commentary. The five ʿŏp̄ālîm / ṭəḥōrîm sites of 1 Sam 5-6 are a single lexical substitution listed in b. Megillah 25b among readings substituted for delicacy; the rendering 'tumors' is governed by the 1-samuel-woh entry `ofalim-tehorim-tumors-1-samuel-5-6`. The anomalous final aleph of hehāləḵûʾ (Josh 10:24) is not a Ketiv/Qere in the source edition and is recorded under the MT-baseline entry. Wave MC, Hebrew part (Josh 3; Judg 7; 2 Sam 6; Editor pass 2026-11-02, claude-opus-5-5) adds four readings; two of them (Josh 3:16; Judg 7:21) depart from the ASV, which follows the Ketiv there. At Josh 3:16 the Qere 'from Adam' makes Adam the upstream point from which the water stood; at Judg 7:21 the Qere makes the Midyanite camp the subject of 'fled'.

entries.standardEnglish: ASV follows the MT at most of these sites; NRSV and other modern versions adopt the versional reading at several (Josh 6:18; 1 Sam 17:4 note; 17:32)
entries.wohChoice: As the founder-ratified Kings entry `mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`: translate the MT vocalization, wording and verse division; give the versional reading in commentary; supply no subject or word the Hebrew leaves unexpressed. Sites in this wave. Joshua: 5:14 'No' (MT lōʾ; some MSS, LXX, Syriac lô 'to him'); 6:9, 13 the subject of 'blowing' left unexpressed (ASV supplies '[the priests]'); 6:18 'lest when you have devoted it' (MT taḥărîmû; LXX 'lest you covet', = taḥmədû); 6:20 MT order of shout and blast, 'they blew' impersonal; 6:26 (LXX adds the fulfilment by Hiel, cf. 1 Kgs 16:34; not translated); 10:10 YHWH as subject of the following verbs; 10:13 the citation of the Book of Yashar (absent from the LXX); 10:15 and 10:43 (absent from the LXX; translated); 10:24 hehāləḵûʾ with anomalous final aleph, translated as the ordinary verb. Judges: 6:7-10 (absent from 4QJudgᵃ; translated); 6:13, 15 the vocalizations ʾăḏōnî 'my lord' and ʾăḏōnāy 'Lord'; 6:14 'YHWH turned to him' (LXX 'the messenger of YHWH'); 13:19 'and he did wondrously', subject unexpressed (ASV '[the angel]'; LXX 'to the Lord who works wonders'). 1 Samuel: 3:13 məqalləlîm lāhem 'bringing a curse on themselves' (a tiqqun soferim; LXX 'speaking evil of God'); 3:21 (LXX longer; not translated); 5:4 'only Dagon was left to him', no supplement (ASV '[the stump of]'); 5:6 (LXX plus on the mice; not translated); 6:19 'looked into the ark' and 'seventy men, fifty thousand men' (LXX 'the sons of Jeconiah'; Josephus and some MSS 'seventy'); 17:4 'six cubits and a span' (LXX, 4QSamᵃ, Josephus 'four'); 17:12 'advanced among men' (Lucianic Greek, Syriac 'in years'); the full MT of 1 Sam 17, including the pluses absent from LXX Vaticanus (vv 12-31, 41, 48b, 50, 55-58), translated without marking; 17:32 'no man's heart' (LXX 'my lord's'); 17:52 'Gai' (LXX 'Gath'). The single departure from the MT in this wave, ratified at human sign-off (2026-11-01) as a narrow exception, 1 Sam 6:18 'the great stone' for MT ʾāḇēl, is governed by the 1-samuel-woh entry `even-ha-gedolah-the-great-stone-1-samuel-6-18`. Wave MC sites. Joshua 3: 3:11 the construct reading 'the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth' (the accents also allow an apposition, recorded); 3:14, 17 the article on the construct hāʾārôn, translated as an ordinary construct. Judges 7: 7:3 'depart from Mount Gil'ad' (emendation 'Gilboa'; the verb ṣāp̄ar uncertain); 7:6 'with their hand to their mouth' kept with the lappers (some LXX witnesses transfer it to the kneelers); 7:8 'provisions' (emendation 'the jars'). 2 Samuel 6: 6:1 wayyōsep̄ translated 'gathered'; 6:2 'from Ba'alei-Yehudah' (4QSamᵃ and 1 Chr 13:6 'to Ba'alah, that is, Qiryat-Ye'arim') and the doubled šēm (single in LXX and 1 Chr 13:6); 6:3-4 the repeated clause (shorter text in LXX and 4QSamᵃ) and 'Achyo' (LXX 'his brothers'); 6:5 'with all kinds of instruments of fir-wood' (1 Chr 13:8, 4QSamᵃ, LXX 'with all their might and with songs'); 6:6 'Nakhon' (1 Chr 13:9 'Kidon') and the unexpressed object of 'reached out' (ASV and 1 Chr 13:9 'his hand'); 6:7 'for his error' (1 Chr 13:10 and 4QSamᵃ differ); 6:22 'in my own eyes' (LXX 'in your eyes').
entries.rationale: Former Prophets wave 1 (Josh 5, 6, 10; Judg 6, 13; 1 Sam 3, 5, 6, 17; Editor pass 2026-11-01, claude-opus-5-5). This entry is shared verbatim by the joshua-woh, judges-woh, 1-samuel-woh and 2-samuel-woh overlays; extend all four together. The Wheel of Heaven Translation translates the Masoretic Text and records ancient-version and conjectural readings in the apparatus (genesis-woh, exodus-woh; the Kings entry, ratified 2026-11-01). At each site listed the MT gives a construable sense, even where most modern commentators prefer another reading: lōʾ in Josh 5:14 can answer 'neither' to Yehoshua's either-or question (Nelson, Joshua, OTL, 1997); taḥărîmû in 6:18 makes sense as 'having devoted (the city), do not then take from it'; the narrator's alternation of the messenger and YHWH in Judg 6:11-24 is characteristic of the malʾaḵ YHWH narratives and is not an error to be harmonized; the tiqqun soferim of 1 Sam 3:13 reads intelligibly as it stands; and the larger figure for Golyat, the asyndetic 'seventy men, fifty thousand men' and the long form of 1 Sam 17 are readings of the transmitted Hebrew whose relation to the shorter or smaller Greek and Qumran readings is a matter of textual history (Barthélemy, Gooding, Lust and Tov, The Story of David and Goliath, OBO 73, 1986; McCarter, I Samuel, AB 8, 1980), which the commentary sets out without adopting. Supplying a subject the Hebrew leaves unexpressed (Josh 6:9, 13, 20; Judg 13:19) would be an interpretive addition, so the line keeps the Hebrew's indeterminacy. Verse numbers follow the Hebrew; in these chapters the English and Hebrew verse divisions agree. Wave MC, Hebrew part (Josh 3; Judg 7; 2 Sam 6; Editor pass 2026-11-02, claude-opus-5-5): in 2 Samuel the Qumran manuscript 4QSamᵃ and the Old Greek often preserve a fuller or better text than the MT (Cross, Parry, Saley and Ulrich, DJD XVII, 2005; McCarter, II Samuel, AB 9, 1984), and modern versions adopt several of their readings in 2 Sam 6. The rule is applied unchanged, because each MT reading of the chapter is construable, and the commentary reports the alternative at each site.

entries.wohChoice: 'YHWH of hosts', as the founder-ratified Kings entry `yhwh-tsevaot-yhwh-of-hosts-kings` and isaiah-woh. Site in this wave: 'in the name of YHWH of hosts, the Elohim of the armies of Yisra'el' (1 Sam 17:45). Wave MC sites: 'the name of YHWH of hosts, who is enthroned on the cherubim' (2 Sam 6:2; 2-samuel-woh yoshev-hakkeruvim-enthroned-on-the-cherubim-2-samuel-6-2); 'he blessed the people in the name of YHWH of hosts' (6:18).
entries.rationale: Former Prophets wave 1 (Josh 5, 6, 10; Judg 6, 13; 1 Sam 3, 5, 6, 17; Editor pass 2026-11-01, claude-opus-5-5). This entry is shared verbatim by the joshua-woh, judges-woh, 1-samuel-woh and 2-samuel-woh overlays; extend all four together. The title is rendered as in Kings and Isaiah, keeping the corpus divine-name style 'YHWH' and the ASV noun 'hosts'. Its grammar (a proper name in apparent construct) and the referent of the 'hosts' (Israel's armies, the heavenly host, the divine assembly) are debated (Mettinger, The Dethronement of Sabaoth, 1982; Cross, Canaanite Myth and Hebrew Epic, 1973), and 'hosts' leaves both open. At 1 Sam 17:45 the title is followed by the apposition 'the Elohim of the armies (maʿarḵôṯ) of Yisra'el', which connects the 'hosts' with Israel's battle lines in David's mouth; the apposition is rendered under the elohim-referent entry (clause 3), and 'armies' keeps the ASV rendering of maʿarḵôṯ used throughout the chapter. The title first occurs in the Hebrew Bible at 1 Sam 1:3, in connection with the Shiloh sanctuary of the ark. Josh 5:14 śar-ṣəḇāʾ-YHWH 'captain of the host of YHWH' uses the singular ṣāḇāʾ and is governed by the joshua-woh entry `sar-tzeva-yhwh-captain-of-the-host-of-yhwh-joshua-5`.

entries.rationale: Former Prophets wave 1 (Josh 5, 6, 10; Judg 6, 13; 1 Sam 3, 5, 6, 17; Editor pass 2026-11-01, claude-opus-5-5). This entry is shared verbatim by the joshua-woh, judges-woh, 1-samuel-woh and 2-samuel-woh overlays; extend all four together. Hebrew prose writes the god's name with the article (habbaʿal), a remnant of its origin as the title 'the Lord'; English treats it as a proper name, and the ASV, NRSV and NJPS omit the article, as Kings does. The spelling with the apostrophe for ʿayin follows the Kings and genesis-woh transliteration practice and governs the theophoric name Yerubba'al, whose explanation in Judg 6:32 (yāreḇ bô habbaʿal 'let Ba'al contend against him') plays on the god's name; the name probably meant 'Ba'al contends' or 'Ba'al is great', and later scribes deformed it to Yerubbeshet (2 Sam 11:21) (Block, Judges, Ruth, NAC 6, 1999). The Ugaritic deity is governed by central baal-ugaritic-baalu-storm-god-cross-corpus-hebrew-bible-polemic, of which this entry is the Hebrew-Bible counterpart.

entries.translit: ʾăšer-niqrāʾ šēm šēm YHWH ṣəḇāʾôṯ yōšēḇ hakkəruḇîm ʿālāyw
entries.lemma: yāšaḇ 'sit, be enthroned, dwell' as participle in the divine title yōšēḇ hakkəruḇîm
entries.partOfSpeech: participle in a divine title; relative clause with resumptive ʿālāyw
entries.literal: who sits (on) the cherubim; over which the name is called
entries.standardEnglish: that sitteth [above] the cherubim (ASV); who is enthroned on the cherubim (NRSV, NJPS); that dwelleth between the cherubims (KJV)
entries.wohChoice: 'which is called by the name, the name of YHWH of hosts, who is enthroned on the cherubim' (2 Sam 6:2): yōšēḇ hakkəruḇîm 'who is enthroned on the cherubim'; ʿālāyw read as the resumptive of the relative ʾăšer ('the ark ... over which the name is called'), rendered by 'is called by'.
entries.rationale: Wave MC, Hebrew part (Editor pass 2026-11-02, claude-opus-5-5). yōšēḇ hakkəruḇîm is a fixed divine title (1 Sam 4:4; 2 Kgs 19:15 = Isa 37:16; Ps 80:2; 99:1; 1 Chr 13:6) that presents the cherubim over the ark as the seat of YHWH's throne, as the central aron-ark-of-the-covenant-ark-of-the-elohim-cross-corpus rationale already states for this verse (Mettinger, The Dethronement of Sabaoth, 1982; Haran, Temples and Temple-Service in Ancient Israel, 1978; McCarter, II Samuel, AB 9, 1984). The central shakhan-dwell-divine-presence-verb-cross-corpus entry renders yāšaḇ 'dwell' in the temple-dedication texts of 1 Kgs 8, where the verb names a residence ('a place for you to dwell in forever'); with the cherubim as object the participle denotes the throne seat, and 'who dwells on the cherubim' would not be idiomatic English. 'enthroned' (NRSV, NJPS) renders the sense without adding anything the title does not say, and the ASV's bracketed '[above]' is not needed. The doubled šēm šēm is kept ('by the name, the name of'), with the possibility of dittography (LXX and 1 Chr 13:6 have one šēm) recorded under mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets; ʿālāyw at the end of the verse resumes the relative ʾăšer, so that the name is 'called over' the ark, the idiom of ownership (Deut 28:10; Jer 7:10-11). The entry is direct.

entries.translit: wayyōsep̄ ; bəḵōl ʿăṣê ḇərôšîm ; wayyišlaḥ ... kî šāməṭû habbāqār ; ʿal-haššal ; wayyiḥar lədāwiḏ ; məḵarkēr ... ʾēp̄ôḏ bāḏ ; ʾešpār ; nāḡîḏ
entries.strongs: H3254/H622 (yāsap̄/ʾāsap̄); H1265 (bərôš); H8058 (šāmaṭ); H7944 (šal); H2734 (ḥārâ); H3769 (kārar); H646 (ʾēp̄ôḏ); H829 (ʾešpār); H5057 (nāḡîḏ)
entries.literal: and he added/gathered; with all woods of cypress; and he sent ... for the oxen let (it) slip; for the error; and it burned to David; whirling ... a linen ephod; a portion (?); leader
entries.standardEnglish: gathered again; with all manner of instruments made of fir-wood; put forth [his hand] ... for the oxen stumbled; for his error; was displeased; danced ... a linen ephod; a portion [of flesh]; prince (ASV)
entries.wohChoice: 6:1 'again gathered' (wayyōsep̄ read as from ʾāsap̄, with ʿôḏ 'again'); 6:5 'with all kinds of instruments of fir-wood' (MT; 1 Chr 13:8 / 4QSamᵃ 'with all their might and with songs' reported), and the ASV instrument names ('harps, psalteries, timbrels, castanets, cymbals'); 6:6 'reached out to the ark' (object unexpressed in the MT; 'his hand' of 1 Chr 13:9 not supplied) and 'the oxen stumbled' (ASV); 6:7 'for his error' (ASV; hapax šal); 6:8 'David was displeased' (ASV); 6:14 'danced', 'a linen ephod'; 6:19 'a portion of meat' (ASV without brackets); 6:21 'prince' for nāḡîḏ (as 1 Kgs 1:35).
entries.rationale: Wave MC, Hebrew part (Editor pass 2026-11-02, claude-opus-5-5). 2 Samuel has the most damaged text of the Former Prophets, and a Qumran manuscript (4QSamᵃ) and the Old Greek often preserve a better text (Driver, Notes on the Hebrew Text ... of the Books of Samuel, 2nd ed., 1913; McCarter, II Samuel, AB 9, 1984; Anderson, 2 Samuel, WBC 11, 1989). The house policy (mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets) translates the MT where it is construable and reports the other readings, and every site here is construable. wayyōsep̄ in 6:1 is pointed as from yāsap̄ 'add', but with an object ('all the chosen men') the sense 'gathered' (ʾāsap̄, LXX synēgagen) is required; the ASV 'gathered again' is kept. In 6:5 the MT 'with all woods of cypress' (bərôšîm; ASV 'fir-wood') is often regarded as a corruption of 'with all might and with songs' (1 Chr 13:8; 4QSamᵃ; LXX); the line keeps the MT. The instrument names are the ASV's, which the corpus already uses at Ps 33:2 (psalms-woh 'harp', 'psaltery'); the modern identifications (lyre, harp, tambourine, sistrum) are given in commentary. In 6:6 the Hebrew has no object for wayyišlaḥ; 'reached out' supplies nothing, while 1 Chr 13:9 and the ASV supply 'his hand'. šāmaṭ (6:6) means 'let drop, release' (BDB), so the oxen either stumbled (ASV, NJPS) or let the cart tilt (NRSV 'shook it'); the ASV is kept and the alternatives, including the canon's 'shook it', are reported. šal (6:7) is a hapax ('error, negligence'), and 1 Chr 13:10 replaces it with 'because he put forth his hand to the ark'. ʾešpār (6:19) is a hapax variously explained as a portion of meat (Vulgate), a cake baked in a pan (NJPS) or a date-cake; the ASV sense is kept. The entry is direct.
